newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakh grain harvest at 11.6 mln T cleaned weight.
newsitem.headline: Kazakh grain harvest at 11.6 mln T cleaned weight.

text.p: Kazakhstan's 1996 grain harvest totalled 11.6 million tonnes cleaned weight, Deputy Prime Minister Zhanybek Karibzhanov told a news conference on Monday.
"The total bunker weight (for 1996) was 13.2 million tonnes while the cleaned weight was 11.6 million tonnes," he said.
Last year's drought-hit harvest was officially around 10 million tonnes, but may have been several million tonnes higher.
The Kazakh government earlier this year revised downward its harvest predictions, cutting forecasts from 18 million tonnes to 16.5 million and then to 13-14 million in September.
But the net figure is line with estimates made by specialists at the Academy of Agricultural Sciences, who had forecast net output at about 11 million tonnes.
"The harvest was carried out in very difficult conditions, and rain and snow in September and October hampered operations," Karibzhanov said.

He said that a shortage of machinery, particularly of combine harvesters, also hit output, while drought in the west of the vast Central Asian nation saw 1.5 million hectares sown to grains lost entirely.
Around 17 million hectares were sown to grains, not including pulses, in 1996, down from 18.8 million hectares in 1995.
Karibzhanov declined to be drawn on harvest predictions for 1997. -- Chris Bird, Almaty Newsroom +3732 509 410
